statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the 21:00 UTC Friday settle and do not reopen inside this horizon, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any published hour and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor. Stress stays in the elevated band because the US-Iran tanker exchange in the Strait of Hormuz is two-sided and unresolved, with the Iranian counter-claim still unconfirmed by CENTCOM, and because the 4 September payroll surprise left hawkish September rate pricing untested by an equity quote.
recommendation: Tail holds a 4-7% closed-venue floor across all 24 published hours, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green throughout. Stress opens at 56%, eases to a 52% low through the dormant overnight window, and rebuilds to a 66% peak as the horizon tracks toward the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen, crossing from the elevated into the high band only in the final two slots. Confidence declines from 85% to 74% as later slots rest on progressively older evidence. No danger window is published, because a closed venue cannot produce the price path the Tail score is defined on.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through the CME weekend halt as the Hormuz tanker exchange stays two-sided and unconfirmed, with WTI near $91.5 after a 9% week and VIX still under 15
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on 6 September, one hour after the final slot of this forecast, so the last print remains the only anchor and no published hour can contain observable price action.

The macro impulse into the halt is hawkish. August non-farm payrolls printed 162,000 against roughly 56,000 expected with the unemployment rate steady at 4.1% and July revised up to -21,000. The 2-year yield rose about 5 basis points to 4.38%, its highest since January 2025, the 10-year added a basis point to 4.776% and the 30-year eased half a basis point to 5.239%. Rate futures moved to price roughly a 59% probability of a hike at the 15-16 September FOMC, up from about 55% before the release. Equities absorbed that repricing calmly: the S&P 500 slipped 0.1% while the Nasdaq-100 held a small gain, and VIX closed at 14.53 inside a 13.80-14.58 range.

The geopolitical sequence is unchanged from the previous assessment and one hour older. US Central Command says American forces struck three Iranian crude oil tankers on Saturday after an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer evaded ballistic missiles fired by the IRGC Navy; the M/T Downy near Kharg Island and the M/T Stark 1 near Jask were permanently disabled and the M/T Kylo was rendered inoperable in the Gulf of Oman. Adm. Brad Cooper framed the action as a tanker-for-tanker economic cost. The IRGC subsequently claimed it had targeted three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels elsewhere, and warned shipping against unauthorised transit. CENTCOM has not confirmed that counter-claim, and no verified follow-on step has been reported in the intervening hour. The campaign is therefore two-sided and unresolved rather than confirmed as an escalation ladder, which is why Stress carries it and Tail does not.

Cross-asset context remains conflicted rather than aligned. WTI is near $91.5 and Brent near $96 after a weekly gain of roughly 9%, an oil-led risk premium that pulls against equities. Friday's internals were rotational rather than one-way: semiconductors led firmly with MU up 6.1%, AMD up 4.7%, INTC up 4.5% and ARM up 3.9%, while AAPL fell 2.5%, MSFT 2.0% and TSLA 5.9%, and delayed index futures closed split with NQ up 0.14% against ES down 0.42% and YM down 0.57%. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and belong in Stress, not in Tail.

Because Tail is defined on a pathological price path and no venue can produce one inside this horizon, Tail is held at a 4-7% closed-venue floor and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON and green in all 24 published hours. Stress is the score that carries the unresolved Hormuz campaign, the oil premium and the untested hawkish rate pricing, and it rebuilds toward the reopen as the unpriced information set grows. Confidence stays high at 85% because levels, yields, volatility, the oil complex, the event calendar and cross-asset internals are all verified and current; the single missing input, a live price path, is structurally unavailable during a halt rather than absent through thin research. The next 7-day calendar is led by PPI on Thursday 10 September and CPI on Friday 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC, ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC that sits beyond this window.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the Friday 21:00 UTC futures settlement and the first twenty-three hours of the CME weekend halt. All 24 slots are available from published Claude assessments, every one is scored at the closed-venue Tail floor of 5% under a normal mode, and every one maps to EA_ON and green. Stress was flat at 38% from the settlement through 10:00 UTC on 5 September, climbed from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 42% by 14:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed, stepped to 48% at 15:00 UTC once the CENTCOM tanker strikes were verified, and rose to 52% by 19:00 UTC and 57% at 20:00 UTC when the Iranian counter-claim was published, easing to 56% at 21:00 UTC as that claim went unconfirmed. Confidence held in a narrow 85-87% band throughout, reflecting a complete evidence set in which only the live price path is unavailable.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, which does not end until 22:00 UTC on 6 September, one hour after the final published slot, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-7% closed-venue floor, easing through the dormant middle of the weekend and widening only as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline; that widening is a gap allowance, not evidence of directional structure. Stress opens at 56%, eases to a 52% low in the quietest overnight hours, ticks up from 06:00 UTC as Gulf and Tel Aviv Sunday cash sessions provide the first equity quotes since Friday, then rebuilds to a 66% peak into Sunday evening, crossing from the elevated into the high band in the final two slots. The drivers are a two-sided and unconfirmed Hormuz tanker campaign, an oil complex up roughly 9% on the week, and hawkish September rate pricing after the 162K August payroll print, none of which has met an equity quote since Friday. Confidence declines from 85% to 74% because later slots rest on progressively older evidence during an actively developing sequence. The reopening auction is the first hour in which structure can be scored: orderly two-way retracement would decay both scores quickly, while repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first genuine Tail amplifier.
